system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Hartwell Libraries' lending policy (from 1 April 2026): membership is free for people who live, work or study in Hartwell, with proof of address; under-12s are registered by a parent or carer; replacement cards cost £2.50. Adults can borrow 12 items (no more than 4 DVDs), children's cards 8, and Housebound Service members 20. Books, audiobooks and magazines go out for 3 weeks, DVDs for 1 week, Quick Reads for 2 weeks, and eBooks for 21 days. Items can be renewed three times unless reserved; DVDs once. Overdue charges are 25p per item per day for adult books and audiobooks and £1 a day for DVDs, capped at £6 per item; children's books carry no overdue charges, and over-65s pay half. Lost or damaged items cost the replacement price plus £3, with the replacement cost refunded if the item turns up within 3 months. Reservations are free for children and 90p for adults, with 7 days to collect. Inter-library loans cost £4 per request, refunded if the item can't be supplied or isn't collected. Accounts owing £10 or more are blocked. Branch Managers can waive charges in cases of hardship, bereavement or library error. Borrowing records are kept for 12 months.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
HARTWELL LIBRARIES — MEMBERSHIP AND LENDING POLICY (Effective 1 April 2026)

1. Membership. Library membership is free to anyone who lives, works or studies in Hartwell. Proof of address is required to join. Children under 12 must be registered by a parent or carer. A replacement card costs £2.50.

2. Borrowing limits. Adult cardholders may borrow up to 12 items at a time, of which no more than 4 may be DVDs. Children's cardholders (under 18) may borrow up to 8 items at a time. Housebound Service members may borrow up to 20 items.

3. Loan periods. Books, audiobooks and magazines: 3 weeks. DVDs: 1 week. Items on the "Quick Reads" shelf: 2 weeks. eBooks and eAudiobooks: 21 days, returned automatically.

4. Renewals. Items may be renewed up to three times, online, by telephone or in person, unless another member has reserved the item. DVDs may be renewed once only.

5. Overdue charges. Overdue charges are based on the type of card used to borrow the item, not the type of item. On adult cards, the charge is 25p per item per day for books and audiobooks and £1 per day for DVDs, capped at £6 per item. No overdue charges are made on children's cards or Housebound Service cards. Children's books borrowed on an adult card are therefore charged at the adult rate. Members aged 65 and over pay half the adult rate.

6. Lost and damaged items. If an item is lost or damaged beyond use, the borrower will be charged the replacement cost shown on the catalogue record, plus an administration fee of £3. If a lost item is found and returned within 3 months of payment, the replacement cost (but not the administration fee) will be refunded.

7. Reservations. Reservations are free for children's cardholders and cost 90p per item for adult cardholders. Members are notified by email or text when the item is ready and have 7 days to collect.

8. Inter-library loans. Items not held in Hartwell's stock can be requested from other library authorities for a fee of £4 per request, payable when the request is made. This fee is non-refundable, including where the item is not collected or the lending library cannot supply it.

9. Blocking of accounts. Accounts with £10 or more in outstanding charges are blocked from borrowing until the balance is reduced below £10.

10. Waiving charges. A Branch Manager may waive charges of up to £10 on an account in cases of hardship, bereavement or library error. Requests to waive charges of more than £10 must be referred to the Library Services Manager, whose decision is final.

11. Conduct. Members must follow the Library Code of Conduct. Membership may be suspended for serious or repeated breaches.

12. Data. Borrowing records are kept for 12 months after an item is returned and then deleted, unless charges remain outstanding.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. How long can I borrow a DVD for?
2. I borrowed four picture books for my daughter on my own adult card and returned them 5 days late. Will I be charged?
3. I paid £4 for an inter-library loan but the other library couldn't supply the book. Do I get my £4 back?
4. After a bereavement, I owe £14 in charges. Can the manager at my local branch waive the whole amount?
response:
1. **DVD loan period:** 1 week. You can renew it **once only**, unless another member has reserved it.

2. **Picture books returned late on your adult card:** Yes, you'll be charged. Charges depend on the card used, not the type of item, so children's books borrowed on an adult card are charged at the adult rate:
   - 4 items × 5 days × 25p = **£5.00**
   - If you're 65 or over, you pay half: **£2.50**
   
   The £6-per-item cap doesn't apply here. Next time, borrowing on your daughter's children's card would avoid overdue charges.

3. **Inter-library loan the other library couldn't supply:** No, the £4 isn't refunded. The policy says the fee is non-refundable, including when the lending library can't supply the item.

4. **Waiving £14 after a bereavement:** Not by your branch manager alone. A Branch Manager can waive up to £10 for hardship, bereavement or library error. Anything over £10 must be referred to the **Library Services Manager**, whose decision is final. Ask your branch to refer it.
   
   While you owe £10 or more, your account is blocked from borrowing until the balance drops below £10.

*Note:* My earlier summary was wrong on three points: it said children's books carry no overdue charges, that inter-library loan fees are refundable, and it left out the £10 limit on branch waivers. The answers above follow the policy document itself.
